sentences.text: The applicant has filed this Application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for enlarging the applicant on Regular Bail in connection with FIR being C.R. No.11214020222051 of 2022 registered with Kamrej Police Station, District:Surat Rural for the offences punishable under Sections 489(a)(b)(c), 406, 420, 201 and 120B of the Indian Penal Code.

2. Heard learned senior advocate Mr.Nirupam Nanavaty with learned advocate Mr.Hardik Dave appearing for the applicant and learned APP Mr.Kanva Antani for the Respondent - State.
3.
Learned advocate for the applicant submitted that the investigation of the offence is over and charge-sheet has been filed.

He submitted that the present applicant has been arrested in the present offence in the month of October, 2022 and since NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/7552/2023 ORDER DATED: 13/06/2024 undefined then the applicant is in custody.

sentences.text: role attributed to the present applicant in commission of the offence is to the effect that the applicant had printed toy-notes in his printing press.
The report of Currency Note Press, Nashik Road, indicates that the notes in question were toy-notes and nothing else.
The notes were to be utilized for the purpose of shooting of movies.
Thus, the notes were not supposed to be circulated in the market nor is there any evidence about these notes having been circulated in the market in any manner whatsoever.
He further submitted that the notes in question bore an indication that all these notes were only for the purpose of entertainment and nothing else.
These notes, in no manner whatsoever, resembled to the genuine currency notes, nor did they contain any security features in them.
The material on which they were printed was also of a substandard quality and the person holding it, would be able to make out that these were not genuine currency notes.
The offences which are alleged in the present FIR and the charge- sheet are not made out against him, since these notes have never been put to circulation.
He, therefore, submitted to allow the present application and enlarge the present applicant on bail subject to suitable conditions.
4. The application is opposed by learned APP Mr.Kanva Antani for the respondent State.
He submitted that the present applicant has well orchestrated the crime and has played a vital role in commission of the offence by printing the currency notes in question.

There is material placed on record to indicate that these notes were not printed for any cinematic purpose, as none of the accused persons were members of any of the organizations associated with film making.

The record also NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/7552/2023 ORDER DATED: 13/06/2024 undefined indicates that these notes were transported and stored in a clandestined manner, which indicates that the purpose behind these notes was not as genuine as is sought to be propagated.
The currency notes which were printed by the present applicant had been used for the purpose of demonstration to lure the public at large for investing their amounts in various schemes.

Thus, the present is an offence,
wherein, counterfeit currency notes have been printed by the present applicant as a part of larger conspiracy to weaken the economy of the country.
He therefore submitted to dismiss the present application.
5. This Court has considered the submissions canvassed by learned advocates for the parties and has also perused the material placed on record.
The record indicates that the co- accused Vikas Padamchand Jain who was the owner of Angadia pedhi namely V.R.Logistics.

The said co-accused met the other co-accused namely Pravin Sukhlal Jain, Dineshbhai Laljibhai Poshiya, Dinanath Ramnivar Yadav etc. at Surat City and it was decided by them to procure huge funds from the public trusts and non-governmental organizations towards investments.

As a part of the said conspiracy,
the branches of V.R.Logistics had been opened at various places across the country.
As a part of the said conspiracy, it was decided that the main accused Vikas Padamchand Jain would make investments of funds for printing counterfeit currency notes.
As a part of the said conspiracy, the co-accused Pravin Sukhlal Jain had entrusted the task of printing of counterfeit currency notes to co-accused Gurmeet Singh and the present applicant.
The applicant who was owning the printing press had in turn printed counterfeit currency notes to the tune of Rs.150 crores of different denominations.

The NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/7552/2023 ORDER DATED: 13/06/2024 undefined material available on record indicates that the co-accused Pravin Sukhlal Jain had sent specimen of counterfeit currency notes to Gurmeet Singh and the present applicant through e-mail.

The number of the currency notes depicted of a specimen, were also found to be the same in the Sagir Ahemad Anishuzzama Khan vs State Of Gujarat on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87376136/
2 counterfeit currency notes, which had been printed by the present applicant.

sentences.text: These currency notes were printed in such a manner that a layman would not know at once that these notes were not genuine.

The report of the RBI indicates that out of 17 features of the genuine currency notes, 14 features of the counterfeit currency notes in question had matched.
6.
It is sought to be contended on behalf of the applicant that these counterfeit currency notes were to be used only for the purpose of filming of movies.
The material available on record indicates that none of the accused persons were ever associated with film industry, nor such orders were ever by the film fraternity to any of them.
The material further indicates that these counterfeit currency notes had been demonstrated by the accused persons to the persons from whom huge investments were expected by them.
Thus, the currency notes in question had already been used by them.
The present offence appears to be a design to make the Indian economy weak for personal gain.
7. Considering all these aspects, no case is made out to exercise discretion in favour of the applicant.
Accordingly, the present Application is dismissed.

(M. R. MENGDEY,J) Manshi Sagir Ahemad Anishuzzama Khan vs State Of Gujarat on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87376136/
